title: Filtering the products table by numbers · part 41

steps.title: Filter then sort: stock = 150
steps.prompt:
Filter first, then ORDER BY tidies what is left.
LIMIT 3 keeps the top of that sorted list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock = 150 ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM products.
Write: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock = 150 ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock = 150 ORDER BY stock LIMIT 3;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE trims, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT cuts.

steps.title: Keep stock != 150
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where stock is not equal to 150.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock != 150;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM products.
Add WHERE after the table name.
Write: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock != 150;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM products WHERE stock != 150;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows stock != 150
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE stock != 150;
hints: Write: SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE stock != 150;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE stock != 150;
